newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - May 5.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's Daily Variety:

* Outperforming most industry expectations, Paramount's "Breakdown" and New Line's "Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery" moved into the top two weekend slots with $12.7 million and $10 million respectively, according to studio projections.
* After less than a year on the job, Robert Cooper resigned as president of Sony Corp TriStar Pictures.
* Michael Jackson, the BBC's director of broadcasting, has been chosen as the new chief executive of Channel 4.

* PolyGram Filmed Entertainment president Michael Kuhn unveiled its new U.S. motion picture releasing company, Polygram Films, to be consolidated with Gramercy Pictures under Polygram Filmed Entertainment Distribution's banner.

* In a major setback for broadcasters, the balanced budget agreement reached Friday by the White House and congressional Republicans counts on the auction of airwaves broadcasters are now using in order to raise $5.4 billion.

* Despite the endless talk about games and entertainment on the Internet, the Hollywood production community has not until now found a truly useful Web application, like special-effects production. A little-known research unit at the Walt Disney Studios, the Multimedia Lab, has perfected a method of compressing data and sending it over the company's internal computer network.
